requirement: Safely manage directory provisioning, atomic swaps, and directory-based mutex locking without TOCTOU race conditions or windows of absence.
skeleton: AtomicDirectoryDeployer class with ensure_directory, safe_remove_directory, acquire_lock, release_lock, and deploy_atomic methods.
caption: A standard-library directory manager built on os, shutil, tempfile, and pathlib that performs each filesystem operation as a single atomic attempt instead of checking first and acting afterwards, with no third-party imports. AtomicDirectoryDeployer resolves base_dir and creates it with parents and exist_ok. ensure_directory creates the named directory with parents and exist_ok, so a concurrent creator never causes a failure. safe_remove_directory calls shutil.rmtree directly and returns True, catching FileNotFoundError to return False when another actor removed the directory first. acquire_lock uses os.mkdir on a name.lock directory as a mutex, returning True when the call creates it and False on FileExistsError, because mkdir is atomic and only one caller can win. release_lock calls os.rmdir and returns False when the lock directory is already gone. deploy_atomic(target_name, build_files) creates a temporary directory with tempfile.mkdtemp inside base_dir itself so it shares the target's filesystem, writes every file into it, creates a temporary symbolic link to it, and swaps that link over the target with os.replace, so the target path always exists and is never deleted before the new version appears; on any failure it removes the temporary directory and re-raises. The fixture injects races and asserts that directory creation survives a concurrent creator, that removal returns False after a concurrent delete, that only one of two lock acquirers wins, that redeploying from v1 to v2 never unlinks the target, and that the temporary directory is created under base_dir.

rationale.teaches: Race-free directory operations: mkdir with exist_ok, catch FileNotFoundError instead of pre-checking, atomic mkdir as a mutex, os.replace with no delete window, and temp dirs on the same filesystem.
rationale.why: Check-then-act code passes every single-threaded test and fails only when another process acts between the check and the act. The fixture injects that interleaving.

candidates.why_wrong: The directory is checked and then created without exist_ok, so a concurrent creator makes mkdir raise FileExistsError.
Removal checks exists and then removes, so a concurrent removal raises FileNotFoundError instead of returning False.
The lock is an exists check followed by mkdir, so two acquirers can both pass the check and both hold the lock.
The old target is deleted before the rename, so there is a window where the deployed directory does not exist.
The temp directory is created in the system temp location, so the final rename can cross filesystems and fail.
